name: Kildare

attributes.attribute: modern name of the Kildare hill

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Kildare is an ancient Irish site. It was first built in Neolithic times. In the seventh century C.E. the Celts made it a provincial capital. The site pairs with the great royal hills Cruachan and Emain Macha, one to the west and one to the north. Today the place is called Knockaulin Hill. Digs at the nearby site Dun Alinne have brought up wide banks and a broad causeway. Workers have also found the foundations of old buildings. The site takes its name from Ailend, an obscure goddess.

okr.objective: Kildare is an ancient Irish capital with a hidden goddess at its heart.
key_results: The site was built in the Neolithic period.
